issues.legal_issue: A timely Letters Patent appeal accompanied by one complete set of required documents is not invalid or time-barred merely because additional sets are filed later.
material_facts: The memorandum of appeal was filed within the prescribed period.
One complete set of the specified documents accompanied the memorandum, and the remaining two sets were filed later, before the appeal was taken up for admission.
issues.conclusion: The requirement to file three sets was directory, and the appeal substantially complied with it; the later filing of the remaining sets cured the irregularity. The appeal was not time-barred.
issues.legal_principle: Order XLI rules 1 and 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure govern the memorandum and accompanying documents for an appeal. The High Court rules on paper books required three typed sets, but, following State of Punjab v. Shamlal Murari, the Supreme Court held that this requirement was directory and that substantial compliance was sufficient. Article 117 of the Limitation Act and the applicable High Court limitation rule governed the time for filing; the High Court’s rule on amendment permitted time for curing procedural defects.

rule.if: letters_patent_appeal and memorandum_filed_within_limitation and one_complete_set_submitted and remaining_sets_filed_later

predicates.letters_patent_appeal: A litigant brought an appeal under a Letters Patent against a judgment of a single judge.
predicates.memorandum_filed_within_limitation: The appellant presented the appeal memorandum within the prescribed filing period.
predicates.one_complete_set_submitted: The appellant submitted one complete set of the required documents with the appeal memorandum.
predicates.remaining_sets_filed_later: The appellant submitted the required additional sets after filing the memorandum.

issues.definition: When a timely Letters Patent appeal is filed with one complete set of the required documents and the remaining sets are supplied later, the appeal is not treated as time-barred.

issues.legal_issue: An application to extend limitation is unnecessary when an appeal was filed within time and the only deficiency was an irregularity in the accompanying documents.
material_facts: The appeal memorandum was filed within the prescribed period, but it was accompanied by only one set of the required documents.
The remaining sets were filed later, and the appeal was complete before it was taken up for admission.
The Division Bench treated the appeal as late and refused to condone delay on that basis.
issues.conclusion: There was no occasion to seek or decide condonation under section 5 of the Limitation Act. The refusal to condone delay, based on the mistaken assumption that the appeal was late, could not stand.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5 of the Limitation Act permits extension where an appeal was not preferred within the prescribed period. The Court held that the considerations governing a section 5 application do not apply when the appeal itself was presented within time and the defect is only an irregularity in its presentation. It therefore set aside the limitation ruling founded on the contrary assumption.

rule.if: appeal_proceeding and memorandum_filed_within_limitation and procedural_defect_only and court_treats_appeal_as_late

predicates.appeal_proceeding: A litigant brought an appeal against a judgment or order.
predicates.memorandum_filed_within_limitation: The appellant presented the appeal memorandum within the prescribed filing period.
predicates.procedural_defect_only: The appeal was timely, but a procedural requirement concerning accompanying documents was not fully met at filing.
predicates.court_treats_appeal_as_late: The court treated the appeal as filed out of time because of the procedural defect.

issues.definition: If an appeal was timely and only had a procedural defect, a dismissal based on treating it as late should be set aside.
